note: Authored conversational knowledge for the internal-intelligence chat engine. Facts that belong to the structured record (metrics, project fields, CV variants) live in credentials.json and are read from there — do NOT duplicate them here. This file holds phrasing, framing, and answers that have no home in the structured schema.

entries.q: What does a development management consultant actually deliver?
entries.a:
Fundable strategies, investment roadmaps, and evaluation systems — documents that survive procurement review and actually get implemented.

Concretely: strategic plans, results frameworks, theories of change, MEL systems, risk-informed development plans, situational analyses, and mid-term reviews. Recent examples include BIRD 2026-2035, a national TVET strategic plan, and a ₱190M climate-smart programme design.

entries.q: Can you work within government or UN procurement systems?
entries.a:
Yes. Engagements have run under government and UN procurement standards across BoI-MTIT, TESDA, MMDA, DOH, ECHO, USAID, World Bank, UNICEF, and WHO.

That includes the documentation side of it — inception reports, milestone-linked deliverables, and the reporting cadence donors expect.

entries.q: What is BIRD 2026-2035 and what was his role?
entries.a:
The **Bangsamoro Investment Roadmap for Development (BIRD) 2026-2035** is the region's decade-long binding investment framework, developed for the BARMM Bureau of Investments under MTIT.

Alvin served as lead technical architect, end to end — framework design, the validation survey platform used to ground it in stakeholder input, and the scoring methodology behind the investment prioritization.

With a 30-minute scoping call. You bring the problem; Alvin brings a structured read on feasibility and the fastest defensible path to a result.

If it's a fit, that becomes a short concept note with scope, timeline, and deliverables before any contracting conversation.

entries.q: What does he mean by systems thinking?
entries.a:
Applied, not decorative. In practice it means mapping causal structure before proposing interventions — causal loop diagrams, stock-and-flow reasoning, and system archetypes such as *Fixes that Fail* and *Shifting the Burden* used to find where a programme's leverage actually sits.

It shows up most visibly in the Complex Adaptive Systems framing of *Seamless Care*, and in how strategic plans get structured around leverage points rather than activity lists.

entries.q: Where is he based and what languages does he work in?
entries.a:
Based in Metro Manila, Philippines (UTC+8), working in **English** and **Filipino**.

Engagements have run across Asia, Africa, and the Pacific, both remote and in-country — including extended fieldwork in BARMM and Mindanao.

**Cognitio+** is the inclusive well-being and digital services platform Alvin founded, built, and architects — operating since 2020.

It's the home for his published resilience work and the digital tools that come out of consulting practice. **ASilva Innovations** is the separate consulting brand under which client engagements are contracted.

entries.q: What monitoring and evaluation work has he done?
entries.a:
Evaluation and MEL work spans mid-term reviews, process evaluations, and results-framework design — including the CONSENT DRR II mid-term review for German Red Cross / Philippine Red Cross, the MOVE UP process evaluation under ECHO, and performance-management system design for DLSU.

There's a dedicated CV variant for this: [MEL CV](Alvin_Silva_CV_Versions/Alvin_Silva_MEL_CV.pdf).

entries.q: Does he design and facilitate training?
entries.a:
Yes — capacity building and facilitation is a 15-year strand of the practice.

That covers full learning-intervention design (session architecture, pre-assessment instruments, facilitator guides), live facilitation for senior government and NGO cohorts, and MHPSS module development for WHO and DOH.

See the [Capacity Building CV](Alvin_Silva_CV_Versions/Alvin_Silva_Capacity-Building-Training_CV.pdf).

entries.q: What happens to what I type here?
variants: what do you do with my data
entries.a:
Nothing leaves your browser. This assistant runs entirely client-side — there's no API call, no server, and no logging of what you type.

The conversation is held in your own browser's local storage so it survives a page reload, and clearing it removes it permanently. Full detail is in the [privacy policy](privacy-policy.html).

entries.q: Is he a development consultant or a tech/private-sector person?
entries.a:
Both, and the combination is the point.

He designs the resilience and investment frameworks (BIRD 2026–2035, CCA-DRR, ₱190M climate-smart programming), **and** builds the technology that executes them (Azure Synapse data warehousing, Power Automate, the MSME AI & Automation Toolkit), **and** knows how to take them to market (*Brand Secrets*, digital growth strategy).

Most development professionals stop at the first. Most technologists never learn the first. Ask about any one of the three.

entries.q: What private-sector and MSME work has he done?
entries.a:
MSME and private-sector work runs across three strands:

• **Investment pipeline design** — BIRD 2026–2035 for BARMM's Bureau of Investments, aligning regional priorities with national PPP guidelines and de-risking private participation.
• **MSME digital enablement** — the *MSME AI & Automation Toolkit* and the *2024 SME Report*, both aimed at cooperatives, CSOs and small enterprises rather than institutions.
• **Startup mentorship** — PhilDev Labs' Financing the Future Challenge, advising early-stage ventures on business modeling, market validation and investment readiness.

Backed by ADB Institute training in financial inclusion and inclusive urban growth.

He builds, not just specifies.

**Data & cloud** — 24 Microsoft Learn modules (17h 28m, 2024): the full Azure Synapse Analytics stack, Data Lake Storage Gen2, modern data warehouse design, and data engineering on Azure.
**Automation & low-code** — Power Automate (including AI Builder and multi-source flows), Power Apps, Power Pages, Power BI.
**Shipped platforms** — DDRiVE-M, Strat Planner Pro, Cognitio+, and the BIRD validation survey platform (offline-capable, PWA).

Grounded further by DAP/SPARTA data analytics certification and NRCP recognition in Data Analytics and Innovation Management.

entries.q: What are his certifications and credentials?
entries.a:
Formal education: **MDM** from the Asian Institute of Management (ADB Scholar) and **BS Social Sciences, Political Science** from UP Visayas.

Selected credentials: **Technology Entrepreneurship: Lab to Market** (HarvardX, 2021), **u.lab: Leading From the Emerging Future** (MITx/Otto Scharmer, 2021), two **ADB Institute** courses on financial inclusion and inclusive urban growth (2021), the **DAP/SPARTA** data analytics track, and **PDRF** business continuity and EOC design.

He is an **Associate Member of the National Research Council of the Philippines** (DOST, 2021), recognized in DRR, Inclusive Growth, Innovation Management and Data Analytics — and served as a **Mentor in the AIM CSO Mentorship Program** (Cycle 6, 2024).

entries.q: Is his security risk management certification current?
entries.a:
Direct answer: **the SRMP-C lapsed.** INSSA certified him as a Security Risk Management Professional – Country level on 17 February 2022, on a three-year term, so it expired 17 February 2025.

The underlying practice didn't lapse with the certificate — security risk management remains a live discipline in his work, alongside PDRF business continuity and EOC design training. But the credential itself should be read as **SRMP-C (INSSA, 2022–2025)**.
